name: Zercher Deadlift
description: A deadlift variation where the barbell is cradled in the elbow crooks rather than held in the hands. The Zercher deadlift shifts loading anteriorly, reduces spinal shear forces compared to a conventional deadlift, and significantly increases core stability demand while still training the entire posterior chain.

execution.starting_position: Squat down and cradle a barbell in the elbow crooks at approximately knee height. Bar is on the floor or set at a low height.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the barbell in a rack at knee height or use it from the floor. Squat down and position the bar in the elbow crooks before lifting.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core and keep the torso as upright as possible.
Step 2: Drive through the floor to stand, extending the hips and knees simultaneously.
Step 3: Lock out at the top with hips and knees fully extended.
Step 4: Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before the pull. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back due to insufficient core bracing
Allowing the elbows to drop, losing the bar
safety_considerations: The Zercher position puts pressure on the forearms — use padding if needed
This is not a maximum-strength lift — use moderate loads
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip and knee extension at lockout. Bar controlled to the starting position on the return.
coaching_cues: Drive the elbows up to hold the bar
